content:
The [Chocolate Toxicity Calculator](/chocolate-toxicity-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Is chocolate poisonous for dogs? Theobromine dose from what was eaten. Enter your dog's weight (kg), chocolate type and amount eaten (grams) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Is chocolate poisonous for dogs? Yes — the theobromine in chocolate is toxic to dogs, and the dose depends on the dog's weight, the type of chocolate and how much was eaten. This calculator works out the theobromine dose in mg per kg of body weight and the risk level, using the published theobromine contents (milk chocolate 2.3 mg/g, dark chocolate 5.3 mg/g, baker's chocolate 16 mg/g, cocoa powder 28.5 mg/g) and the published dose bands. This is an estimate only — not veterinary advice. If your dog ate chocolate, call your vet immediately, especially for anything above a mild dose.

## How to use the Chocolate Toxicity Calculator

Start by entering your dog's weight (kg), then choosing your chocolate type from the list and finally entering your amount eaten (grams). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your dog's weight in kilograms.
2. Pick the type of chocolate and how many grams were eaten.
3. Read the dose, the risk level — and call your vet if it is anything above mild.

## Formula

Dose (mg/kg) = grams eaten × theobromine per gram ÷ dog's weight in kg. Under 20 mg/kg is mild, 20–40 moderate, 40–60 serious, over 60 potentially fatal.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Chocolate Toxicity Calculator](/chocolate-toxicity-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 15 kg dog that eats 100 g of milk chocolate takes in 230 mg of theobromine — 15.3 mg/kg, a mild dose. The same amount of cocoa powder would be 190 mg/kg, a severe dose. Try the same figures in the [Chocolate Toxicity Calculator](/chocolate-toxicity-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Dog's weight (kg): 15, Chocolate type: Milk chocolate, Amount eaten (grams): 100), the [Chocolate Toxicity Calculator](/chocolate-toxicity-calculator) returns Theobromine dose: 15.33 mg per kg of body weight, Total theobromine: 230 mg, Risk level: Mild, What to do: Mild dose — an upset stomach or vomiting is possible. Keep an eye on your dog and call your vet if symptoms appear.. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. ## Why chocolate is toxic to dogs

Chocolate contains theobromine, a stimulant dogs break down far more slowly than humans do. It builds up in their system, overstimulating the heart and nervous system. Dark chocolate and cocoa powder are far more dangerous than milk chocolate because they contain much more theobromine per gram — 100 g of cocoa powder carries more theobromine than 1 kg of milk chocolate.

## Symptoms to watch for

Vomiting and diarrhoea usually come first (within 6–12 hours), then restlessness, excessive thirst and panting, a rapid heart rate, tremors and, at high doses, seizures. Symptoms can take hours to appear, so do not wait for them — call your vet as soon as you know chocolate was eaten, and tell them the dog's weight, the type and the amount.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Call your vet immediately — do not wait for symptoms to appear.
- Tell the vet the dog's weight, the chocolate type and the amount eaten.
- Dark chocolate and cocoa powder are far more dangerous than milk chocolate.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much chocolate is toxic to a dog?

It depends on the dog's weight and the chocolate type. Under 20 mg of theobromine per kg of body weight is mild; over 60 mg/kg is potentially fatal. A 15 kg dog eating 100 g of dark chocolate is already at a moderate dose. Try it with your own numbers in the [Chocolate Toxicity Calculator](/chocolate-toxicity-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### My dog ate chocolate — what should I do?

Call your vet immediately, even if your dog seems fine — symptoms can take hours to appear. Tell them the dog's weight, the chocolate type and how much was eaten. Try it with your own numbers in the [Chocolate Toxicity Calculator](/chocolate-toxicity-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is white chocolate dangerous for dogs?

Barely — white chocolate has only about 0.25 mg of theobromine per gram. It can still upset a dog's stomach, but it is far less dangerous than milk, dark or baker's chocolate. Try it with your own numbers in the [Chocolate Toxicity Calculator](/chocolate-toxicity-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Chocolate Toxicity Calculator use?

Dose (mg/kg) = grams eaten × theobromine per gram ÷ dog's weight in kg. Under 20 mg/kg is mild, 20–40 moderate, 40–60 serious, over 60 potentially fatal.
